title: Variable Frequency Drive (VFD)
model_title: Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) — 6-Pulse Rectifier, DC Link, IGBT Inverter

introduction.definition: A variable frequency drive controls an AC motor's speed by changing the frequency and voltage it supplies. A rectifier makes DC, a DC link smooths it and an IGBT inverter switches it with pulse-width modulation (PWM) to synthesise AC of any frequency.
key_points: Soft start and controlled stop built in

classification.type: Voltage-source inverter, 6-pulse diode front end, IGBT PWM

introduction.summary: A variable frequency drive (VFD, inverter) controls the speed of an AC motor by changing the frequency and voltage it supplies. The rectifier turns mains AC into DC, the DC link capacitors smooth it, and the IGBT inverter switches the DC rapidly (PWM) to build a new AC waveform of any frequency. Running pumps and fans at reduced speed instead of throttling saves a lot of energy (affinity laws: power ∝ speed³).

working_principle.characteristic_curve: Constant V/f (or vector control) up to base speed; field weakening above. Pump/fan power falls with the cube of speed.

waveforms.title: Waveforms: AC → DC → PWM → motor
waveforms.description: The rectifier turns fixed-frequency AC into DC; the capacitors smooth it. The IGBTs switch the DC on and off thousands of times per second (PWM) so the average voltage follows a sine wave of any chosen frequency. Motor speed ≈ 120 × f / poles, so changing f changes speed.

video_tutorials.title: Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Variable Frequency Drive (VFD).
A variable frequency drive controls an AC motor's speed by changing the frequency and voltage it supplies.
A rectifier makes DC, a DC link smooths it and an IGBT inverter switches it with pulse-width modulation (PWM) to synthesise AC of any frequency.
Typical applications include pumps and fans (energy saving); conveyors and process lines; compressors; cranes and hoists (with braking).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Motor (speed follows the VFD) – Rotor, Shaft & Speed Marker Disc.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) works.
Mains AC passes the line reactor into the rectifier, which turns it into DC.
The DC link capacitors smooth the DC voltage.
IGBTs switch the DC thousands of times per second (PWM) to build a sine-like AC of the chosen frequency.
The motor speed follows the output frequency — watch the motor ramp up and down.
The control board sets speed, ramps and protection; the fan cools the heatsink.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
The rectifier turns fixed-frequency AC into DC; the capacitors smooth it.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Variable Frequency Drive (VFD).
Check fan and heatsink temperature; read fault log.
Clean filters and heatsink; check terminal torque.
Replace cooling fans and DC capacitors (end of life).
Watch for overcurrent / overvoltage trips: drive trips. Common cause: too-short ramps, motor fault, regenerative load.
Watch for overheating: over-temperature trip. Common cause: blocked filters, failed fan, high ambient.
Watch for DC-link capacitor failure: ripple, bus faults. Common cause: age, heat.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
